clue.text: Something other than TV corporation flipping microphone switch?

indicators.note: flipping turns the whole run of pieces over, so the string they make together is read from its far end

parts.note: to be something other than a thing is not to be it
the tube is old slang for television
corporation is jocular slang for a paunch, a tum

explanation.surface: A gadget that is not the BBC's, toggling a microphone on and off?
explanation.walkthrough: NOT, TUBE and TUM run together make NOTTUBETUM, and 'flipping' turns that whole string end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: The control that silences a microphone is the button labelled mute.

clue.text: Bridge article on odds

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the article follows the odds

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds on a horse
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece on bridge, the card game, published with the betting odds.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridge a gap is to span it, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Larceny's right for a banking standard

indicators.note: one letter standing in for another: R takes the place of A

parts.note: larceny is theft, stealing

explanation.surface: A thief's justification for a bank's rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterling silver is a fixed standard of purity, and sterling is the British currency held by banks.

clue.text: Grand passage provides proof

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
an alley is a narrow passage between buildings

explanation.surface: An impressive corridor offers evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proof' is the printer's sense, not evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley, or galley proof, is a printer's trial print set up for correction before page make-up.

clue.text: Ruler discovered in wings of chintz armchair

indicators.note: the wings of something are its two sides, so each word gives only its outermost letters

explanation.surface: A monarch found hiding in the wings of a chintz-covered armchair.
explanation.walkthrough: A wing armchair has wings, which is why the image sits so well.
explanation.definitionFit: A czar, also spelt tsar, was the emperor ruling Russia.

clue.text: Ruined actor, openly gay after universal pressure

indicators.note: after places the actor and gay pieces behind the universal and pressure letters

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal
P is the symbol for pressure in physics
a thesp, short for thespian, is an actor
out means openly declaring that one is gay

explanation.surface: A performer brought down after coming out under widespread pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Up the spout is British slang for ruined or done for.

clue.text: Habit of word use in commercials?

indicators.note: the word use appears within the world of commercials, so it follows the advert piece

parts.note: an ad is a commercial, an advertisement
diction is choice and use of words

explanation.surface: Asks whether the language of adverts is a matter of habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit in the sense of a dependency one cannot shake, such as a drug habit.

clue.text: Root canal finally stops teeming

indicators.note: the letter stops up the word, sitting inside it like a plug

parts.note: rife means teeming, abundant

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word canal

explanation.surface: Dental treatment: the end of a root canal plugs a gap where trouble is rife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Root canal' is a dental phrase, but 'Root' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To root, or root through, is to rummage or search, as one rifles through a drawer.

clue.text: Large degree of noise obscuring December's false report

parts.note: L is the clothing abbreviation for large

indicators.note: obscuring hides the month, so its letters vanish from the unit of loudness

parts.note: a decibel is a unit measuring loudness
Dec is the abbreviation for December

explanation.surface: Loud noise drowns out a December lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Libel is a published statement that is false and damages a reputation.

clue.text: Vigour of macho types caught in flying formation, say

indicators.note: in places the macho types and catch inside the formation

parts.note: birds or aircraft often fly in a V shape, spelt out as vee
he-men are macho men
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Tough guys flying in V formation show great energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehemence is forceful intensity, a close synonym for vigour.

clue.text: Mischievous imp sure can help out scrapping sons

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, here standing for the plural too

explanation.surface: A naughty sprite certainly lends a hand, getting rid of the boys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrapping' takes the S out of SURE CAN HELP; 'out' rearranges the remaining ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A leprechaun is a mischievous little sprite from Irish folklore.

clue.text: Prison's no answer with time in dump

indicators.note: no means without, so the answer letter is dropped from the prison

parts.note: a jail is a prison

explanation.surface: A prisoner with no answer doing time in a squalid place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dump' looks like a noun, a squalid place, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To jilt a lover is to dump them abruptly.

clue.text: Socialist author, otherwise sensible

parts.note: or means otherwise, as in 'hurry or you'll miss it'
well means sensible or advisable, as in 'it would be well to wait'

explanation.surface: A left-wing writer described as sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell, author of Animal Farm, was a committed democratic socialist.

clue.text: Asian anger slightly turned around since The King and I?

indicators.note: around wraps the turned word about the other pieces
turned means the word for mild anger is read backwards

parts.note: to irk is to annoy, to anger slightly
as can mean since, as in 'as it rained, we stayed in'
HM is His Majesty

explanation.surface: Someone from Asia gets a little cross since watching the musical The King and I.
explanation.walkthrough: KRI goes round ASHMI, splitting as K...RI.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kashmiri is a person from Kashmir, a region of South Asia.

clue.text: Strands (carried across by shuttle) with effect from start of Thursday

parts.note: w.e.f. is the abbreviation for with effect from

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Threads on a loom, effective from Thursday.
explanation.definitionFit: The weft is the set of crosswise threads carried through the warp by the loom's shuttle.

clue.text: Trouble follows lewd cop film

parts.note: dirty means lewd or smutty
to harry is to harass or trouble

explanation.surface: Trouble comes after a filthy police movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty Harry is the 1971 Clint Eastwood police thriller.

clue.text: A place for variety, often involving upright lives and everything

indicators.note: involving means surrounding the reversed piece

parts.note: much can mean often, as in 'do you go there much?'

indicators.note: in a down entry, upright means written upwards, reversed

parts.note: is means lives or exists
all means everything

explanation.surface: A venue for variety acts, often with lively entertainments.
explanation.definitionFit: A music hall was a theatre staging variety shows, a popular British entertainment.

clue.text: Met base people generally on a thoroughfare

parts.note: they means people in general, as in 'they say'
Rd is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Officers met at the base, with people out on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Met' is London's Metropolitan Police, not the past tense of meet; its headquarters is Scotland Yard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yard, short for Scotland Yard, is headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police.

clue.text: Resignation speech written in red without intro being all over the place

indicators.note: the speech is written inside the cut colour
without its intro, the first letter of the colour word is dropped

parts.note: ruby is a deep red
'I quit' is what one says when resigning

explanation.surface: A resignation letter written in red ink, everywhere at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Ubiquity is the state of being found everywhere at once.

clue.text: My job is a balancing act, making progress while strung out

definitions.text: My job is a balancing act, making progress while strung out

parts.words: My job is a balancing act, making progress while strung out
parts.note: a performer speaks: balance is the whole job, moving forward on a stretched line, with strung out also hinting at being drunk, tight

explanation.surface: A stressed worker describes juggling everything while exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strung out' suggests stress or drugs; read literally it is a rope stretched taut.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus performer who walks a taut rope high up must keep perfect balance while advancing.

clue.text: Piece lifted to obtain valuable fragment

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifted means turned upwards, reversed

parts.note: a piece is slang for a gun
to get is to obtain

explanation.surface: Raising a gun to get a precious bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a lump of gold, or figuratively a precious morsel of information.

clue.text: One's discounted starchy tubers and starchy grass

parts.note: salep is a starchy flour from dried orchid tubers
rice is a cereal grass with starchy grains

explanation.surface: A list of starchy foods in a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: SALEP is an obscure word for a starchy meal of orchid tubers.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduced price in a sale is the discounted one.

clue.text: Spurning Congress customarily when former partner stands for American

indicators.note: one piece substituting for another in the word

parts.note: as usual means customarily
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Snubbing Congress as usual, when an ex runs in place of the American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' is sexual congress, not the US legislature.
explanation.definitionFit: An asexual person has no sexual attraction, so spurns intercourse.

clue.text: With determination, I get close to home

parts.note: near means close
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Determined, I head nearer to home.
explanation.definitionFit: In earnest means seriously and with firm resolve.

clue.text: Thrill excited fiery Celt

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered Celt gets stirred up and thrilled.
explanation.definitionFit: To electrify an audience is to thrill or excite it.

clue.text: Spiritless state, maybe, gets heat taken off with unknown brand of cognac

indicators.note: taken off means removed from the front of the word

parts.note: heathenness, being a heathen, may be called a state lacking spirit in the religious sense
taken as written
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A dry US state loses its warmth with an unknown brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spiritless state' suggests a dry US state; it is a state of being, without religious spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Hennessy is a leading cognac house in France.

clue.text: Warming Arctic may become so fierce, spoiling one of Earth's extremes

indicators.note: spoiling ruins the order of the letters, mixing them up

parts.note: E is the first letter, one end, of the word Earth

explanation.surface: Global warming could spoil the Arctic, a fierce pole of the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: If Arctic warming continues the polar sea may become clear of ice.

clue.text: Perhaps more disturbing volume excluded from upcoming exam preparation

indicators.note: excluded from means taken out of the word
in a down entry, upcoming means read upwards, reversed

parts.note: revision is studying for an exam

explanation.surface: Revising before an imminent exam without volume might be more upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversing REVISION gives NOISIVER, and the V is then dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Louder is one way of being more disturbing, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Police officer and corporal entering school

indicators.note: entering means going inside

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: A policeman and a soldier start at school.
explanation.walkthrough: PC Plod is the policeman in Enid Blyton's Noddy books, British slang for a plodding constable.
explanation.definitionFit: PC Plod is a jokey British nickname for an ordinary police constable.
